title: WHAT IF EARTH'S OCEANS DRAINED?
foot: SIMULATION · STYLISED GLOBE · NOT REAL GEOGRAPHY
display: three thousand six hundred and eighty-two meters
ten thousand nine hundred and thirty-five meters

segments.heading: PULL THE PLUG
segments.text: What if someone pulled the plug on every ocean on Earth?

segments.heading: THE SEA DROPS
segments.text: The water starts to fall. On average, it's three thousand six hundred and eighty-two meters deep.

segments.heading: HIDDEN MOUNTAINS
segments.text: Underneath is the longest mountain range on Earth. Nearly sixty-five thousand kilometers of volcanoes.

segments.heading: DEEPER THAN EVEREST
segments.text: In the Pacific, a trench drops ten thousand nine hundred and thirty-five meters. Everest fits inside.
segments.event: NOAA Challenger Deep 10,935 m; Everest 8,849 m.

segments.heading: THE REAL TALLEST
segments.text: And the tallest mountain isn't Everest. From the seafloor, Mauna Kea rises ten thousand two hundred meters.
segments.event: Guinness: Mauna Kea ≈10,205 m base to peak, 4,205 m above sea level.

segments.heading: STILL UNMAPPED
segments.text: Most of this landscape has never been mapped in detail. Less than a third.

segments.heading: ALL THE WATER
segments.text: And all of Earth's water, rolled into one ball? It's less than fourteen hundred kilometers wide.
segments.event: USGS: sphere ≈ 860 mi (1,384 km) diameter, 1.386 billion km³.
